<h2 title="Class RoutingOptions" class="title">Class RoutingOptions</h2>
</div>
<div class="contentContainer">
<ul class="inheritance">
<li>java.lang.Object</li>

<div class="description">
<ul class="blockList">
<li class="blockList">
<hr>
<pre>public final class <span class="typeNameLabel">RoutingOptions</span>
extends java.lang.Object</pre>
<div class="block"><p>The options defines how a route should be calculated.
 <p>The options are used for all transport modes and engines.
 <p>** Electric vehicle specific requirements **
 Electric vehicle consumption are estimated when at least one consumption model is defined.
 Currently two models are supported:
 <ul>
 <li>PhysicalConsumptionModel
 Aside from the values in PhysicalConsumptionModel additionally these values needs to be defined:
 <ul>
 <li><code>RoutingOptions.transport_specification.vehicle_specification.current_weight_in_kilograms</code></li>
 <li>Additionally <a href="sdk-for-android-explore-api-reference-waypoint#currentWeightChangeInKilograms"><code>Waypoint.currentWeightChangeInKilograms</code></a> can be defined.</li>
 </ul>
 </li>
 <li>EmpiricalConsumptionModel</li>
 </ul>
 <p>By setting <a href="sdk-for-android-explore-api-reference-electricvehicleoptions#ensureReachability"><code>ElectricVehicleOptions.ensureReachability</code></a> the <code>RoutingEngine</code> inserts additional charging stations
 to reach the waypoints.
 This feature requires setting the <a href="sdk-for-android-explore-api-reference-batteryspecifications" title="class in com.here.sdk.routing"><code>BatterySpecifications</code></a>.
 By default a vehicle might not reach the waypoint, when the initial charge is not enough to reach all waypoints.
 See the parameter description below for more details.
 <p><strong>Note:</strong> This is a beta release of this feature, so there could be a few bugs and unexpected behaviors.
 Related APIs may change for new releases without a deprecation process.</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>

<a id="transportSpecification">
<!--   -->
</a>
<ul class="blockList">
<li class="blockList">
<h4>transportSpecification</h4>
<pre>@NonNull
public&nbsp;<a href="sdk-for-android-explore-api-reference-transportspecification" title="class in com.here.sdk.transport">TransportSpecification</a> transportSpecification</pre>
<div class="block"><p>Defines the transport specification which contains the transport mode and the vehicle specifications
 for the transport mode chosen.
 By default generic vehicle specifications for the chosen transport mode are used.
 <strong>Notes:</strong>
 <ul>
 <li>The transport mode <code>TransportMode.PUBLIC_TRANSIT</code> is not supported.</li>
 <li>It is highly recommended to define the <code>truckCategory</code> that is being used, if the <code>transportMode</code> is
 set to <code>TransportMode.TRUCK</code>.</li>
 <li>The <code>TransportSpecification.vehicleSpecification.occupancy</code> won't have effect if HOV and/or HOT lane
 usage is not allowed using <a href="sdk-for-android-explore-api-reference-evtruckoptions#allowOptions"><code>EVTruckOptions.allowOptions</code></a>.</li>
 <li>The <code>TransportSpecification.pedestrianSpecification.walkSpeedInMetersPerSecond</code> if present, will be
 used by the service as the walking speed for pedestrian routing. It influences the duration of walking
 along the route. The provided value must be in the range [0.5, 2.0]. When the value is outside this
 range, an invalid parameter error is raised. Refer to <a href="sdk-for-android-explore-api-reference-routingerror" title="enum in com.here.sdk.routing"><code>RoutingError</code></a> for details. The
 default speed is 1 meter per second.</li>
 </ul></div>
</li>
</ul>
